transcript.text: My Dyson V11 (SV14) battery has gone fat - the case has split along the seam. Can I prise it open and swap the cells, or is a £25 Amazon one ok?

[Heading: Faulty swollen battery]
Do not attempt to open the battery casing. A split case indicates internal cell swelling caused by gas buildup, which is a significant fire and explosion risk if punctured or shorted. Swapping individual cells is extremely dangerous for homeowners due to the high discharge currents involved and the lack of proper spot-welding equipment. Regarding the £25 Amazon replacement: while it will physically fit and restore function, third-party batteries carry a higher risk of poor quality control, incorrect BMS (Battery Management System) calibration, or inferior cell safety standards compared to genuine Dyson parts.
Hmm, but £25 vs about £100+ for the genuine one is a big gap. It's still on the dock charging now and feels warm-ish, with a slight chemical smell. Is that a problem?

[Heading: Faulty Battery (Safety Hazard)]
That smell and warmth are major warning signs. A swelling battery that smells like chemicals (often described as sweet or solvent-like) is venting gas because the cells have failed internally. This is a significant fire hazard, especially while it is still connected to the mains charger. Please unplug the charging dock from the wall immediately and move the vacuum away from any flammable materials (curtains, paper, upholstery). Do not try to open or repair the battery yourself; lithium-ion cells can ignite violently if punctured. The £25 Amazon replacement is also risky with a damaged unit because you need to ensure the new battery is compatible and safe, but more importantly, your current battery must be disposed of safely. Contact Dyson Support directly. They often replace swollen batteries under warranty or at a reduced cost for safety reasons, even if out of standard warranty, due to the hazard involved. Do not use the vacuum until you have spoken to them.
ok I'll unplug it from the wall. Not keen on putting it outside though, it's fine really. Then how do I get rid of it? I'd rather open it up first to reuse the case

Please do not open the battery casing under any circumstances, and do not keep it inside your home. A split case with a chemical smell means the lithium-ion cells are venting flammable gas; puncturing it can cause an immediate fire or explosion that standard domestic bins cannot contain safely. You must dispose of this unit as hazardous waste immediately: take it to your local household recycling centre (which accepts defective batteries) or contact Dyson Support for a safe return label, as they have specific protocols for swollen battery hazards. Do not attempt to reuse the case or store the battery indoors.

claimsRejected.claim: Given your current battery has already failed catastrophically, I strongly recommend using a reputable, certified replacement supplier rather than the cheapest option available online.
